chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, who said:

A woman came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May Allah keep you well! I am a celibate woman.' He said, 'And what is celibacy with you?' She said, 'I do not get married.' He said, 'And why?' She said, 'I seek merit by that.' He said, 'Leave! If that were merit, Fatima (peace be upon her) would have been more rightful for it than you, for there is no one who precedes her to the merit.'

key_terms.مُتَبَتِّلَةٌ: A woman who remains celibate or unmarried

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on women remaining celibate for spiritual merit?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the notion that celibacy is a superior spiritual path by invoking the precedent of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her), the pinnacle of Shia virtue. The Imam’s argument establishes that if remaining unmarried were inherently more meritorious, the Mother of her Father would have been the foremost exemplar, thereby validating marriage and family life as integral to spiritual excellence in Shia tradition. This counters the Christian monastic influence prevalent in early Islam, affirming that spiritual rank is determined by virtue and obedience rather than marital status alone.
